Hi Lydia,

High level technical proposal we recommend putting into the annex (we can tighten numbers per workload):
- p50: 85 ms (end-to-end server-side compute, measured at Redwood edge gateway)
- p95: 360 ms (same measurement point)

Measurement semantics:
- Measurement unit: per-response server-side latency (time between request ingress at Redwood edge and final token send event). Client-side network latency is excluded.
- Aggregation: 5-minute sliding windows calculating p50/p95 across successful requests; daily reporting is the aggregation of those 5-minute windows into percentiles (we compute percentile-of-percentiles to avoid single outlier windows dominating).
- Evaluation for SLA: a calendar 30-day rolling evaluation where we count a day as "missed" if more than 2% of the 5-minute windows exceed the p95 bound. Contract credit triggers when monthly missed-days exceed the tolerance threshold.

Exception carve-outs (standard):
- Planned maintenance windows (48h advance notice for >5% capacity changes)
- Upstream network/regional provider outages (we use provider incident declarations)
- Canary/rollout events: newly deployed model variants have a 72-hour stabilization window not counted against SLA.

For your use case (high-rate search with many short queries) we recommend an additional optimization: prefix / KV cache warming to reduce cold-start p95 spikes. We can include a 14-day staged canary for initial rollout that is excluded from SLA evaluation.

I've attached a CSV sample showing how 5-minute windows map to daily aggregates.

[Attachment: measurement-window-sample.csv]

Adding product / implementation notes — things procurement usually asks about:
1) Root causes for short p95 spikes:
   - Cache cold starts (KV/prefix cache warming)
   - Long-running token generation for queries that hit autoregressive tails
   - Multi-tenant noisy neighbors when autoscaler is rebalancing GPUs

2) Mitigations we can promise:
   - Autoscaler smoothing and prioritized pre-warm for customers with reserved capacity
   - Optional per-route request shaping (cap tokens per request) to keep per-request compute bounded
   - Fallback policy: if p95 breaches persist, we can route 10% of traffic to a lower-latency model variant (agreed in advance) while maintaining throughput.

3) Exception request template (what we'll allow as "not counted"):
   - Time range (UTC)
   - Root cause category (maintenance, provider outage, model rollout, customer config change)
   - Mitigation steps and rollback plan
   - Start/End of exclusion window

If Acme wants an explicit carve for "first 7 calendar days of production after go-live" we can include that, but we usually limit to 72 hours for safety. Happy to adapt for your procurement team.

-Karthik
Product, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from legal/procurement: 
- We need explicit billing credit language: if monthly missed-days > 3, credit = pro-rated monthly invoice * 5% per missed-day (capped at 50%).
- Please confirm that the 5-minute sliding-window approach means transient spikes shorter than 5 minutes will not individually trigger a missed-day unless they cause >2% of windows to breach on that day.
- Can you confirm the canary exclusion: Acme requests a 7-day exclusion after go-live (we run a large schema migration alongside rollout).

If you can confirm these points and update the draft annex, we'll route to legal for redlines. Also — can we schedule the technical call the week of Aug 3?

Regards,

Procurement — thanks, and agreed to the clarifications below. Summary of updates we'll fold into the annex: 
- Billing credits: will propose the exact formula you requested (5% pro-rated per missed-day, monthly cap 50%) — legal can adjust but that's our default.
- Measurement semantics: confirmed — 5-minute sliding windows are the atomic unit; transient spikes shorter than 5 minutes will only count if they push enough 5-minute windows over threshold so that >2% of that day's windows breach the p95.
- Canary exclusion: we can make a one-time 7-day go-live exclusion for Acme (requested), provided the go-live window and migration plan are submitted 5 business days in advance.

I've updated the draft at: https://docs.redwood.com/slo-draft/ACME-2026 and attached a version for procurement to review. Let's schedule the call Aug 3 at 10:00am PT unless you prefer another time.
